meta.theme: the reform that would separate a grade's reporting function from its motivating function refused on the ground that each is the other's condition, since what a mark records is conduct while the mark was at stake and a mark nobody will consult stops moving anybody, which replaces the question of how to separate them with the question of what rate of exchange a scheme is accepting, and makes the test of a scheme what behaviour it pays for

meta.reviewer_notes: The received view is stated warmly and at length so that its accompanying reform is available as a wrong answer to the purpose question. The two critique paragraphs are deliberately asymmetrical in difficulty, the first conceptual and the second observational, and the second of them carries its claim in a closing sentence after a vivid observation about pupils, which makes an option built from that observation the strongest distractor in the set. 2026-10-03 CAT-size pass: 642→510 words, 5→4 paragraphs, 5→4 questions. Merged the closing choice (p5) into the change of question (p4), cutting its restatement of the new question, and tightened the rest; dropped q5 (inference that restates the second half of the purpose question from the same closing sentences).
meta.tone: practical, unromantic, faintly impatient with reform

quality.adversarial_review: Q1's live rival is the option that the passage exists to show grades measure less about ability than people think, which is a premise of the second paragraph and not the point, since the passage goes on to argue that the stake is what makes the record worth having. Q2's rival is the option naming what a pupil produces when nothing turns on it, which is exactly what the paragraph says you are left with once the consequence has been removed; it is offered there as the loss, and called the less informative of the two, rather than as the thing a grade records. Q3's rival is the option that the third paragraph establishes how much more strategic pupils are than their teachers, which borrows the paragraph's most memorable observation and mistakes evidence for the claim it was brought in to prove, since the paragraph's closing sentence says the motivating power of a grade is borrowed from the reporting. Q4's rival is the private quiz shown to nobody, which satisfies the motivating half and removes the later reader on whom the argument depends. Q5's rival is the option about weighting the final examination, which takes one item from the passage's list of exchanges and turns it into the recommendation the passage refuses to make. (2026-10-03, CAT-size pass: q5 was dropped, so any note above about it no longer applies.)

passage.title: What the Mark Is Paying For

paragraphs.text: Everybody who defends grading says two things about it, and both are true. A grade is a message to people the pupil will never meet: next year's teacher, the admissions office, the employer with forty applications and one afternoon. It compresses three terms of work into a letter or a number. A grade is also what gets the essay written by Thursday. The standard complaint follows: the two jobs pull against each other, since what is fair to a later reader is not always good for the pupil in front of you. So does the standard reform: separate them. Let the comment teach and the mark report, and keep the comment clear of the mark so that it is read.

The reform is more expensive than it looks, because the separation destroys the thing it was meant to protect. Ask what a grade actually records. It is not a measurement of a capacity, in the way a ruler measures a table. It is a record of what this pupil did while the mark was at stake: by a date, under a rule about how much help was allowed, with a consequence attached. Take the consequence away and the same exercise measures a different quantity, namely what somebody produces when nothing turns on it. For most of the purposes a transcript is read for, that is the less informative of the two. An employer is not trying to find out what an applicant can do in ideal conditions.

The dependence runs in the other direction as well, and this half is easier to observe. A mark moves anybody only while it is believed to matter, and it is believed to matter because somebody is going to read it. Marks that will never be consulted lose their hold within a term. Pupils are extremely good at working out which assessments go on the record and which are practice, and they redistribute their effort accordingly, without discussion. So the motivating power of a grade is not a property the grade has on its own. It is borrowed from the reporting.

If that is right, the two functions are not two jobs sharing an instrument, and separating them is not a tidying operation but an amputation. Each is the other's condition. What follows is a change in the question. The useful question is not how to tell informing from motivating, but what rate of exchange between them a scheme accepts, since every scheme accepts one. A single final examination buys comparability across pupils and across years, and pays in a fortnight of cramming and in everything three hours cannot examine. Continuous assessment buys steadiness and pays in a record that is partly a record of the household. Generous marking buys goodwill and pays in a signal nobody outside the school can read. None of these exchanges is avoidable, which is exactly why they should be made deliberately rather than inherited. So the question to ask of a scheme is what behaviour it pays for, and whether that is the behaviour anybody wanted to measure.

questions.target_mistake: naming the premise of the second paragraph, that a grade is not a measurement of ability, as the point of the passage
questions.prediction_target: The learner should be able to say before looking: show that the two functions need each other, and replace the reformer's question with a different one.
questions.stem: The author's chief purpose in the passage is

options.A: to recommend that schools report a mark and a comment separately, and to explain how
options.B: to show that grades reveal less about a pupil's ability than is commonly believed
options.C: to show that a grade's two functions depend on each other, and to say what a school should therefore be asking
options.D: to compare the grading schemes now in use and identify the one that distorts least

explanation.expert_notice: The last paragraph states both halves of the passage's work in consecutive sentences: each function is the other's condition, and what follows is a change in the question. It ends by putting the new question in the form a school can use, asking what behaviour a scheme pays for.
explanation.correct_reasoning: The correct option carries the argument and its consequence. The middle paragraphs establish the dependence in both directions, the record needing a stake and the stake needing a reader, and the last converts that into a different enquiry from the reformer's. A purpose that stops at the dependence leaves the new question unexplained, and one that names the reform leaves the whole of the critique unexplained.
explanation.question_type_note: An author-purpose question wants a verb and an object. In a passage that replaces one view with another, the replacement belongs inside the purpose, not outside it.
explanation.reading_habit: Count the paragraphs a candidate purpose accounts for. An option that describes only the criticism has named a stage of the argument, and a passage that criticises almost always goes on to say what to do instead.

distractors.why_wrong: This is the standard reform as the first paragraph reports it, and the second paragraph opens by calling it more expensive than it looks and the fourth calls it an amputation. The passage never explains how to carry it out because it is arguing that it cannot be carried out without loss.
distractors.seductive_element: The reform is stated last in the opening paragraph, in the author's own voice and with no marker of distance, so a reader who fixes the purpose early carries a reported proposal away as a recommendation.

distractors.why_wrong: This is a premise rather than the point. The second paragraph denies that a grade measures a capacity in order to say what it does record, conduct while the mark was at stake, and the rest of the passage is built on the value of that record rather than on its limitations.
distractors.seductive_element: It is the most quotable claim in the passage and the one most likely to be remembered, and scepticism about grades is what a reader expects an essay on the subject to be selling.

distractors.why_wrong: Three schemes are named, each with what it buys and what it costs, and none is preferred. The paragraph's own sentence says the useful question is about a rate of exchange, which is a framework for choosing rather than a choice.
distractors.seductive_element: The list of schemes reads like the beginning of a comparison, and readers expect an argument about trade-offs to end by picking the best available bargain.

questions.target_mistake: taking the passage's denial that a grade measures a capacity for a claim that it records nothing worth having
questions.stem: According to the passage, what a grade records is

options.A: a measurement of the pupil's ability, of the kind a ruler gives for the length of a table
options.B: the pupil's performance at a moment when nothing in particular turned on it
options.C: the teacher's considered estimate, however provisional, of what the pupil will manage later
options.D: what the pupil did with the mark at stake, by a date and under a rule about help

explanation.expert_notice: The second paragraph puts the question and answers it in two consecutive sentences. A grade is not a measurement of a capacity, in the way a ruler measures a table; it is a record of what this pupil did while the mark was at stake, by a date, under a rule about how much help was allowed, with a consequence attached.
explanation.correct_reasoning: The correct option is that second sentence. The detail is load-bearing rather than decorative, since the whole case against the reform rests on it: if what gets recorded is conduct under a stake, then taking the stake away changes what is being measured, which is the paragraph's next move and the reason the separation is called expensive.
explanation.question_type_note: A detail question about what something is turns on the sentence saying what it is, not the sentence saying what it is not. Both are usually present, and the denial usually comes first.
explanation.reading_habit: When a passage tells you what something is not, read the next sentence with particular care. Authors clear the ground with a denial and put the claim you actually need immediately afterwards.

distractors.why_wrong: The paragraph denies precisely this, saying a grade is not a measurement of a capacity in the way a ruler measures a table, and then saying what it records instead. The ruler is the passage's own image, used to rule the reading out.
distractors.seductive_element: It is what a grade looks as though it ought to be, and borrowing the passage's own comparison makes the claim feel supported by the very sentence that rejects it.

distractors.why_wrong: This is what the paragraph says you are left with once the consequence has been removed, offered as the loss rather than as the thing recorded, and it is called the less informative of the two for the purposes a transcript is read for.
distractors.seductive_element: It is the live rival, because it uses the paragraph's own machinery and sounds like the sober deflationary reading that a sceptical passage seems to invite.

distractors.why_wrong: No estimate of future performance appears anywhere, and the teacher's own judgement is never discussed. What the passage says is recorded is something the pupil did, on a date, under a rule about help, with a consequence attached.
distractors.seductive_element: Predicting later performance is what the outside readers named in the first paragraph actually want a grade for, so a reader supplies the purpose in place of the content.

questions.target_mistake: reading the paragraph as a remark about how strategic pupils are, when its job is to turn the dependence round
questions.prediction_target: The learner should be able to say: the paragraph before showed a record needing a stake, and this one shows the stake needing a reader.
questions.stem: The third paragraph chiefly serves to

options.A: show the dependence running the other way, from the reporting to the motivating
options.B: concede that the reform criticised earlier would work in some schools after all
options.C: explain why pupils distrust marks that are not awarded under examination conditions
options.D: establish that pupils are more strategic about assessment than their teachers are

explanation.expert_notice: The paragraph announces itself in its opening clause, saying the dependence runs in the other direction as well, and it closes by naming that direction: the motivating power of a grade is not a property the grade has on its own, it is borrowed from the reporting.
explanation.correct_reasoning: The correct option names the reversal, which is what makes the argument work. The paragraph before established that a record is worth reading because a consequence was attached when it was made; this one establishes that the consequence is felt only because somebody will later read the record. Both directions have to be in place before the next paragraph can say that each function is the other's condition, so an option that stops at the pupils' behaviour has taken the evidence for the claim it supports.
explanation.question_type_note: A paragraph-function question in the middle of an argument is usually answered by asking what this paragraph adds to the one before it.
explanation.reading_habit: When an author writes that something runs in the other direction as well, expect a mirror image of his previous claim, and check that you can state both halves separately before moving on.

distractors.why_wrong: Distrust is never described, and examination conditions are not the paragraph's subject. What pupils are said to work out is which assessments go on the record, which is a judgement about who will read a mark rather than about how it was sat.
distractors.seductive_element: The passage does treat examination conditions seriously elsewhere, and a paragraph about pupils weighing up assessments invites an account of what they think of them.

distractors.why_wrong: No concession appears here. The paragraph supplies the second half of the case against the reform, and the next paragraph hardens the verdict further by calling the separation an amputation rather than a tidying operation.
distractors.seductive_element: Arguments of this shape usually do concede something in the middle, and a reader expecting the pattern will read a change of direction as a change of side.

distractors.why_wrong: The pupils' skill is reported and no comparison with teachers is made anywhere. Their accuracy about which marks count is evidence for a claim about where a mark's motivating power comes from, and the paragraph's closing sentence states that claim rather than any claim about who understands assessment better.
distractors.seductive_element: It is the live rival, because the observation about pupils is the paragraph's most memorable sentence, and a vivid piece of evidence is easily mistaken for the point it was brought in to prove.

questions.target_mistake: applying the argument to an assessment that has only one of the two functions the argument requires
questions.prediction_target: The learner should predict the two conditions before looking: a stake on the person assessed, and a record somebody later will consult.
questions.stem: On the author's account, which of the following is an assessment in which both of a grade's functions are present?

options.A: a private diagnostic quiz whose results are shown to nobody except the pupil
options.B: a national survey of reading ability administered to a sample of schools and reported yearly
options.C: a licensing examination whose result is recorded and consulted by employers
options.D: a rehearsal in which a conductor stops the orchestra to correct a difficult passage

explanation.expert_notice: The argument needs two things present at once, and the passage names both. There must be a consequence attached to the performance, which is what makes the record a record of conduct under a stake, and there must be somebody later who will read it, which is what makes the stake credible to the person being assessed.
explanation.correct_reasoning: The correct option is the only case in which both conditions hold. The result is recorded and later read by people the candidate will never meet, so the reporting function is present; and because it is read, it carries a consequence for the candidate, so the motivating function is present and borrowed from the reporting exactly as the third paragraph describes. Every claim in the passage can then be applied to it without adjustment.
explanation.question_type_note: A scope question is answered by listing the conditions the argument requires and then testing each case against the list. Here two conditions have to hold at once, and three of the cases satisfy only one.
explanation.reading_habit: Write the argument's conditions down as a checklist before reading the options. Cases that satisfy one condition and not the other are the standard distractors, and they are invisible until the list exists.

distractors.why_wrong: Nobody later reads it, which removes the reporting function outright, and on the passage's own account removes the motivating one too, since a mark that will never be consulted loses its hold within a term. Neither function is present, so the case cannot be one in which both are.
distractors.seductive_element: It is the live rival, because it is unmistakably a school assessment and it looks like the reformer's ideal, which makes it feel like the passage's natural subject.

distractors.why_wrong: The unit assessed is a school system rather than a person, and no individual carries a consequence or appears in any record. Nothing in the passage about what a pupil does while the mark is at stake has anything to attach to.
distractors.seductive_element: It is an educational measurement whose results are certainly read by later audiences, and the reporting half of the passage's machinery seems to be present.

distractors.why_wrong: No record is produced and nothing is graded, so the passage has no purchase on it. Correction during practice is the one situation the argument says nothing about, since the whole account concerns what a mark does when it is written down.
distractors.seductive_element: It is the clearest case of feedback separated from assessment, which is precisely the arrangement the reform in the first paragraph was reaching for.

vocabulary.passage_use: It compresses three terms of work into a letter or a number
vocabulary.meaning_here: reduces a large body of material to a very small token

vocabulary.passage_use: not a tidying operation but an amputation
vocabulary.meaning_here: a removal that costs the whole of a function

vocabulary.passage_use: buys comparability across pupils and across years
vocabulary.meaning_here: the property of results that can fairly be set beside one another

mentor.challenge: A familiar reform is described so sympathetically that you may not notice it belongs to somebody else. Watch for the sentence where the author starts costing it, because the whole argument is that the two things the reform would separate cannot survive apart.
mentor.one_sentence_summary: The reform that would split a grade's reporting function from its motivating one fails because each is the other's condition: what a mark records is what a pupil did while the mark was at stake, so removing the stake changes the quantity measured, and a mark nobody will consult stops moving anybody within a term, which means the real question about a grading scheme is not how to separate the two functions but what rate of exchange between them the scheme is accepting, and therefore what behaviour it pays for.
mentor.main_idea: Grades both inform later readers and get the work done, and the usual proposal is to separate the two jobs. They cannot be separated. A record is worth reading because a consequence was attached when it was made, and a consequence is felt because somebody will read the record. So every grading scheme is buying one thing and paying in another, and the choice a school is actually making is which behaviour its marks will pay for.
mentor.simple_explanation:
People who defend grades say two true things. First, a grade is a message to strangers: next year's teacher, an admissions office, an employer with forty applications and one afternoon. It squeezes three terms of work into a single letter. Second, a grade is what gets the essay written by Thursday.

Then comes the usual complaint: those two jobs fight each other, because what is fair to a stranger reading later is not always what is good for the pupil in front of you. And then the usual fix: split them up. Let comments do the teaching and let the mark do the reporting, and keep the comment away from the mark so that somebody actually reads it.

The author says this fix costs far more than it looks. Start with what a grade really records. It is not a measurement of ability the way a ruler measures a table. It is a record of what this pupil did when something was riding on it: by a deadline, under rules about how much help was allowed, with a consequence at the end. Take the consequence away and you are measuring something else, namely what somebody produces when nothing depends on it. For most of the reasons people read a transcript, that is the less useful of the two. An employer is not trying to find out what you can do in perfect conditions.

Now the same dependence the other way round, which is easier to see. A mark only moves anybody while it is believed to matter, and it is believed to matter because somebody is going to read it. Marks that will never be looked at stop working within a term. Pupils are superb at working out which assessments go on the record and which are just practice, and they quietly move their effort accordingly. So a grade's power to motivate is not really the grade's at all. It is borrowed from the reporting.

If that is right, these are not two jobs that happen to share one tool. Each one keeps the other alive, and splitting them is not tidying up; it is cutting something off. So the question changes. Stop asking how to keep the informing and the motivating apart, and ask what exchange rate between them a particular scheme is accepting, because every scheme accepts one. A single final exam buys comparability between pupils and between years, and pays for it with a fortnight of cramming and by ignoring everything that cannot be tested in three hours. Continuous assessment buys steadiness and pays with a record that is partly a record of the home the pupil goes back to. Marking generously buys goodwill in the room and pays with a signal that nobody outside the school can read.

None of those trades can be avoided, which is exactly why they should be made on purpose instead of inherited. So the question to ask about a grading scheme is: what behaviour is this scheme paying for, and is that the behaviour anybody wanted to measure?
mentor.why_difficult: The opening paragraph states a proposal with real warmth and no marker of distance, so readers carry the reform away as the author's own and then find the rest of the passage arguing against them. The second difficulty is the direction of the dependence, which runs both ways and is easy to hold in one direction only: a record needs a stake, and a stake needs a reader. The third is the fourth paragraph, which names three grading schemes and sounds like a survey, when its job is to show a single claim applying three times.
mentor.author_intention: To take a reform the reader already half believes in, show that it cuts through a dependence rather than a tangle, and leave him with a harder and more useful question to put to any scheme he meets.

paragraph_journey.note: A grade informs strangers and gets the work done, the two pull against each other, so the usual proposal is to separate them.
A grade records what a pupil did with something at stake. Remove the stake and you measure a different thing, and the less useful one.
A mark moves people only while somebody will read it. Pupils know exactly which marks count. The motivation is borrowed from the reporting.
The functions are each other's condition, so ask what exchange a scheme accepts. Every scheme buys one thing and pays in another, so choose on purpose and ask what behaviour it pays for.

mentor.tone_progression: It opens generous towards the view it is about to dismantle, becomes analytic and slightly clinical while the dependence is established in both directions, turns brisk at the list of exchanges, and ends practical and demanding, handing the reader a question rather than an answer.
key_transitions: 'The reform is more expensive than it looks, because the separation destroys the thing it was meant to protect.' (opening of paragraph 2): the received proposal is turned into the target.
'It is borrowed from the reporting.' (end of paragraph 3): the second half of the dependence is stated in five words.
'What follows is a change in the question.' (paragraph 4): the replacement arrives and the reformer's question is set aside as unanswerable.
mentor.misunderstanding: The commonest wrong model is that the passage is against grades, since it says a grade is not a measurement of ability and that every scheme distorts behaviour. It is not: the whole argument depends on the record being worth having, and the distortion is presented as the price of something bought rather than as a scandal. The second wrong model treats the reform in the first paragraph as the author's proposal, which turns the next three paragraphs into an argument the reader cannot place. The third takes the fourth paragraph's three schemes for a recommendation in progress and waits for a winner that never arrives.
mentor.traps_summary: This set offers the reported reform as the purpose, a premise as the point, a list of illustrations as a survey of schemes, what is left once the stake is removed as the thing recorded, a piece of evidence as the point it was brought to prove, and an assessment with only one of the two required functions. Asking whether a claim keeps both directions of the dependence answers three of the four.
mentor.reading_lesson: When an author says two things depend on each other, establish the direction of each dependence separately and write both down, because every question in such a passage will test whether you kept both, and the strongest distractors keep one and drop the other. The companion habit is to treat a list of examples inside an argumentative paragraph as evidence for the claim stated just before it: authors name three cases to show a claim holding three times, not to begin a comparison.
mentor.real_world: The same question is worth putting to any measure that is both a record and an incentive: a hospital's published waiting times, a call centre's handling averages, a researcher's publication count, a driver's safety score. In each case the honest enquiry is not whether the number informs or motivates, since it always does both, but what behaviour it pays for, and whether anybody chose that behaviour on purpose.
mentor.takeaway: A mark records what somebody did when it mattered, which is why it cannot be made not to matter and still be worth reading.
mentor.reflection_question: Which number that is kept about your own work is also the thing that decides how you spend your week?

eli10.big_idea: A grade's two jobs, reporting and motivating, depend on each other, so the real question is what behaviour a grading scheme rewards.
eli10.story: A grade does two jobs. It tells strangers, like a college or an employer, how a pupil did. It also makes pupils work. Many people say these jobs clash, so they want to split them. Let comments teach and marks report. The writer says the split would break both jobs. A grade records what you did when it counted: by a deadline, with a consequence. Remove the consequence and you measure something weaker. And a mark only pushes you to work if someone will read it. Think of cricket practice and a real match. Players try hardest when the score goes on record. So each job needs the other. Every grading scheme gains something and pays something. One final exam makes pupils easy to compare, but it brings cramming. The writer says to choose the trade on purpose. Ask what behaviour the scheme pays for.
paragraphs: States the usual view: grades inform strangers and make pupils work, so reformers want the two jobs split.
Objects: a grade records what a pupil did with something at stake; without the stake it means less.
Turns it round: a mark only motivates while someone will read it, so motivation is borrowed from reporting.
Draws the lesson: each job needs the other, every scheme pays a price, so ask what behaviour it rewards.
eli10.author_view: The writer is practical and a little impatient with easy reforms: he values grades but wants schools to choose their trade-offs on purpose.
